title: Reservation schema in PostgreSQL
idea: The schema stores each reservation as a time range on one table, and an exclusion constraint makes PostgreSQL refuse any two active ranges that overlap on that table.

analogy.text: A shared calendar that will not let two events sit on top of each other in the same room column. Cancelled events fade out and stop blocking.
analogy.breaks: Two writers can arrive at once; PostgreSQL makes one wait, then refuses it.

points: `dining_table` and `reservation` map Table and Reservation; Table is a reserved SQL word.
`slot` is a `TSTZRANGE`, so the half-open interval from Java fits one column.
`EXCLUDE USING gist` refuses overlaps per table, only for CONFIRMED and SEATED rows.
Best-fit selection runs in SQL; a lost race returns 23P01 and the caller retries.

steps.caption: Three parties of four ask for 19:00 at once. Free four-plus tables: T2, T3, T4.
Each transaction runs the best-fit query. All three see T2 as free.
All three insert on T2. One gets in first; the others wait on its row.
The first commits. The waiting inserts now overlap a committed row and fail with 23P01 (or 40P01 on a deadlock).
The losers roll back and run the query again. Now T3 is the best fit; one wins it.
The last party retries once more and lands on T4. No table was ever double booked.

code.caption: The schema on a real PostgreSQL 18, then six writes. The database alone decides which ones are refused.

walk.text: `btree_gist` lets one gist index compare TEXT ids with `=`. Enums are TEXT with a CHECK.
A reservation has a party size, a non-empty time range, a status and a unique key.
The core invariant: no two active ranges overlap on the same table.
One index serves the host's list by start time; a partial one serves the no-show sweep.
A helper inserts one reservation with a range built from two times.
Overlap, back-to-back, bad party, unknown table, reused key, and rebooking a cancelled time.
Print ok or the Postgres error code and the constraint that stopped it.

code.title: Best fit with retry
code.caption: Three parallel bookings compete for the same best table. A trimmed schema keeps the race short.

walk.text: Four tables and the same exclusion constraint as the full schema.
Only overlap losses and deadlocks are retried; other errors surface.
Best fit in SQL: smallest table that seats the party with no active overlap.
No candidate means NO_TABLE; otherwise insert the 90-minute range and commit.
A 23P01 means another party won this table: roll back and choose again.
Three parties in parallel, then a fourth party and a couple, one at a time.
Count rows per table to prove each table holds one 19:00 booking.

pitfalls: Do not trust a NOT EXISTS check alone; two transactions can both pass it.
Limit the exclusion constraint to active statuses, or cancelled rows block rebooking.
Retry only on 23P01 or 40P01, with a cap; other errors are real failures.

quiz.q: What does book.mjs print for the fourth party of 4?
options: a fourth party of 4 gets: T4
a fourth party of 4 gets: NO_TABLE
a fourth party of 4 gets: BUSY_TRY_AGAIN
a fourth party of 4 gets: T2
quiz.why: T2, T3 and T4 each hold an active 19:00 range. No free table seats four, so the best-fit query returns no row.

takeaway: Let an exclusion constraint forbid overlaps; retry the loser on the next table.
